I haven't written `skills/migration-dry-run/SKILL.md` yet. The writing-skills skill says to read its references before drafting the frontmatter and body, and I haven't done that. I'm reading them now, along with the full baseline file, so the counters quote the agents' exact words rather than my summary.

Here is how I plan to use them:

- **Form:** The baseline shows agents that know the rule and skip it under pressure (14 of 20 runs). That calls for a prohibition, a rationalization table and a red-flags list. The bulletproofing reference covers how to write those.
- **Description:** It will start with "Use when..." and give only the triggers, such as applying a migration to staging or any shared environment. It won't summarize the workflow, so agents can't take the description as a shortcut and skip the body.
- **Rationalization table:** It will have one row for each of the three excuses you saw ("staging is disposable", "only additive", "dry run takes too long"), plus any others in the full baseline file.
- **Frontmatter:** I'll set `name`, `description` and `license` after checking the exact rules in `discovery.md`.

Once I've read the files, I'll write the file and show it to you. Then I'll re-run the same four scenarios with the skill present to check that the agents comply. Any new rationalizations that turn up go into the REFACTOR pass.
